blocks.heading: Conflicting objectives
blocks.text: Objectives conflict when pursuing one makes another harder to achieve. Conflict can occur between groups or within one group’s priorities. Raising wages can reduce short-term profit if other conditions are unchanged; reducing prices may help customers but leave less money to cover costs. A conflict is not proof that cooperation is impossible: changes in productivity or a negotiated compromise may help several groups.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Workers at Omuti Foods request higher pay while customers resist a price rise and the owners need to maintain cash for repairs. Paying more without extra revenue increases costs and can reduce the funds available for repairs. Passing the full increase to customers may reduce sales. A phased wage change combined with feasible waste reduction could ease the conflict, but the savings must be achievable. The explanation must connect each objective to a constraint rather than merely list that groups want different things.
